items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Charlie Hawkins; the interviewer mentions him in a narrative about Robert (inaudible) and Nancy Wilson.

ctx.x: And he had Lou Donaldson on alto, so Robert (inaudible) had a drummer named Charlie Hawkins and Charlie Hawkins left Robert (inaudible) and he went over to the Blue Morocco -- then it was called Ann's Red Rose and one night he said, Ches, I want you to hear a young lady sing and it happened to be Nancy Wilson. And at the time she was typing in an office building during the week and working on weekends at Ann's Red Rose.
Well, Pearl Bailey worked at the Blue Morocco, too, in her early days and I worked at the Fat Man's you know when it opened across the street?
